items.title: TALON
items.subtitle: Self-hosted multi-agent AI system
items.summary: Started as an AI job-search pipeline and grew into a self-hosted multi-agent platform: a model gateway, a mixture-of-agents engine and CI/CD, with a human approving every outward action.
bullets: Original pipeline: job APIs, LLM scoring, Gmail OAuth, Telegram alerts, CRM sync, a network graph and daily reporting, shipped in phased releases.
Added a LiteLLM model gateway that routes between local Ollama models and cloud models, a mixture-of-agents engine and a CI/CD pipeline.
Human-in-the-loop by design: it reads and drafts but never sends email or applies to jobs on its own.
Now the base for a multi-agent security research demo in an independent study at IU Indianapolis.

items.title: This portfolio
items.subtitle: A latent space you can fly through
items.summary: Every bright point here is a real project, role, award or skill, placed by its meaning: a Python pipeline embeds each description and UMAP folds the space into 3D.
bullets: Build time: Python embeds every item (sentence-transformers MiniLM), reduces to 3D with UMAP and writes one JSON file.
Run time: Next.js and react-three-fiber draw the cloud with custom GLSL shaders; GSAP ScrollTrigger and Lenis turn scroll into a camera flight.
The search box embeds your query in the browser: instantly with TF-IDF, or with the same MiniLM model that placed the points if you opt in to deep search.

items.title: ANTA
items.subtitle: Autonomous Network Triage Agent
items.summary: ANTA replaces the binary network alert with a graded trust score for every network segment. Two cooperating agents read the traffic and challenge each other's evidence, and the score says how much to trust a segment and why. This is the design and evaluation plan for my Security Engineering course project; the pipeline is the next thing to build.
bullets: Two specialized agents read TShark output: one checks protocol conformance, the other behavioral timing.
Each agent challenges the other's evidence. Findings that survive set the score, and disagreement counts as uncertainty instead of being averaged away.
Trust is a subjective-logic opinion (belief, disbelief, uncertainty), fused into one Trustability and Performance Resilience Score per segment.
A remediation module drafts iptables and ufw rules for a human to review. Nothing is applied automatically.

sections.title: The problem
sections.body: Signature-based and threshold-based detection tools bury analysts in alerts, and many of those alerts are false positives. A binary alert says "malicious" or "benign" and nothing about confidence. An analyst can't tell whether a flag rests on one weak signal or on several that agree, and can't watch a segment recover after an incident. ANTA computes trust and justifies it instead.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: ANTA works in four stages, from raw packets to a per-segment assessment.
items: Ingestion. TShark parses live or captured PCAP traffic and extracts protocol fields and timing features for each segment.
Protocol Conformance Agent. It checks traffic against what the protocol expects and reports deviations, such as malformed fields or sequences a compliant implementation wouldn't produce.
Behavioral Timing Agent. It looks at intervals and bursts and reports how far a segment drifts from its normal pattern.
Adversarial evaluation loop. Each agent gets the other's evidence and challenges it. A finding stands only if it survives, and disagreement between the agents goes into the score.
sections.note: Because the two agents look at different aspects of the same traffic, one agent's false positive is less likely to be confirmed by the other.

sections.title: The trust score
sections.body: Each agent turns its evidence into a subjective-logic opinion about the segment: belief that it is trustworthy (b), disbelief (d) and uncertainty (u), with b + d + u = 1. When there is little evidence, uncertainty stays high, so a segment isn't called safe or hostile on thin data. The two opinions are fused with a consensus-style operator, and the score is the probability expectation of the fused opinion, where a is the base rate:
sections.note: Disagreement between the agents is treated as extra uncertainty, which pulls the score toward the base rate, so conflicting signals produce a cautious score instead of a confident one. The score is recomputed as new traffic arrives and older evidence is down-weighted, so a segment earns trust back gradually after an incident. The input weights and the decay rate are not fixed yet; they will be set and tested during evaluation.

sections.title: Remediation, with a human in the loop
sections.body: When a segment's score drops, ANTA drafts iptables and ufw rules scoped to the flagged host or subnet, so the response stays narrow. The rules are never applied automatically. A wrong block can cut off legitimate users, and the score expresses graded trust, not certainty, so a human reviews every rule.

sections.title: Evaluation plan
items: Data. CICIDS2017 PCAPs. Monday's benign-only traffic gives the baseline for normal scores, and the attack days test whether scores fall during attacks and recover afterward.
Metrics. Precision, recall and false-positive rate for detection, plus how the score behaves across the attack days: how early it drops, how far, and how it recovers.
Baseline. A single-agent version of ANTA with the debate loop removed, to isolate what cross-examination adds.

sections.title: Limits and ethics
items: CICIDS2017 was generated on a testbed, so results may not carry over to production traffic.
LLM agents can produce explanations that don't match the evidence. The debate step is meant to reduce that, but it can't be assumed to remove it.
Running several agents over every segment adds latency and cost that a live deployment must budget for.
Packet captures contain sensitive data, so ANTA should run only on traffic the operator is authorized to inspect.

sections.title: What's next
sections.body: Implement the pipeline and test it on CICIDS2017 against the single-agent baseline. Later: testing on live capture, agents for other layers, and studying how the score weights and recovery rate should be set for different environments.

items.title: Healthcare AI platform
items.subtitle: Predicting appointment no-shows
items.summary: A three-tier microservice system that predicts which patients are likely to miss appointments, so a clinic can act before the revenue is lost. A dashboard flags high flight-risk patients, backed by a Node.js orchestrator and a Python service that serves a scikit-learn Random Forest model.
bullets: Presentation: a Next.js 15 dashboard with client-side filtering and risk-tiered alerts for patients whose predicted no-show probability is above 0.7.
Logic: a Node.js and Express orchestrator that runs the PostgreSQL queries and calls the AI service over REST.

Intelligence: a FastAPI service wrapping a serialized scikit-learn Random Forest. Inputs include the lead time between booking and appointment, age and gender, and prior no-show history when available.
Data: a PostgreSQL schema with Admin, Staff and Doctor roles ready for access control, plus a seed script that generates 600+ mock patient records. No real patient data.
